Guys. I have a small secret for you. It helps me. If you want to earn money on the market, the first - you have to learn losing money. It is true - to lose money without any control. Our problem - we want to control trading. It is impossible. The first- using knowledge of RTM site and min lot (0.01 and less) - do deals in order to lose money. I guarantee you - about maybe 10-20 deals we lose money and then you start to earn. Why?- our control disappers.

Hey Alex, I totally agree with you.

I have been following a pretty well-known trader trade live 3 days a week via twitter feed here in the states. Although I think her price reading doesn't hold a candle to S/D price reading, she's a perfect example of someone who believes it down in her soul that as a trader she MUST of necessity have small, well-managed losses.

Her reasoning is that if she's wrong, she wants to know it right away, take the loss and move on or wait for another entry. It's really quite intriguing to follow her live twitter feeds Tues-Thurs NY session. She can have 6 losses in a row and then have two winners that completely wipe-out her losses and end up in profit by noon. Furthermore, she believes that it is impossible to trade emotion-less - that it is normal to have emotion. She's just one who appears to have become really good at not allowing her emotions to sabotage her focus.

Lastly, I posted screen shots pointing out that she was buying into untested fresh supply, and into areas where there was a bearish QM setting up. She politely commented back and said she did not care. Again, a perfect example of a trader who doesn't deviate from a set plan.

HI RTM traders!

I would like to share my experience in journey to business FOREX. This is not a game, by studying the material on this website you can get your real business. I began my journey about 4.5 years ago. Purely by chance, having learned from the Internet, I decided to try it. I visited one-month free courses in my city, but with the obligatory opening of Live account in the broker's club. After the course I opened the account with $ 2,000 on it. As I understand how, I was lucky because a month later I returned $ 2700. It became even more interesting, I realized that I can make money fast and even faster. Two months later, I already had $ 500 on my account, and I stopped trading, knowing that something was missed. My first cognition was the study of indicators. Within 1 year I reviewed 1000 indicators, changed their parameters, and finally I realized that everything was useless and I just spent a year out of window. I didn’t trade for almost a year, so I did not spend my deposit.

Then I accidentally (though nothing happens by chance) came across a book “Trading Chaos” by Bill Williams. I studied the theory, practice, and I realized that since then I was ready to trade successfully. I do not want to criticize this theory and Bill Williams, on many sites is it written that this strategy made his family multimillionaire, but I had no luck, unfortunately or fortunately, but I wasted my deposit.

At that moment I gave up Trading for three months and, honestly, I was ready to forget about the case. Once on the Internet, since the 21 century is a century of the Internet, I ran against an article about the schedule and Elliott wave analysis. I was very inspired and found immediately the books on Wave Analysis, no need to list them here as those, who were fond of the Wave Analysis, know these books well. You know, I was lucky, my second deposit began to grow, and for 6 months I was a profitable trader. I was happy more then ever. I participated at the forums on wave analysis, I began to notice that five Wavers have 5 different versions of market analysis for wave analysis. At first I did not take it seriously, but then I felt uneasy, when the wave analysis began to falter in my analysis. Each proved his case, so did I, and, as it seemed to me, each got a point. I ended in a deadlock... I started to make mistakes, and almost spent second deposit. I realized that although Wave Analysis is really good kind of analysis, I'm probably out of luck. So, 3 years passed.

A friend of mine advised me a well-known site FF, and I got to the Thread J16. I was inspired again, studied, dug and delved. I liked the understanding of the market, but I was not mentally ready to trade, even though I really liked the thread J16 and still like it. I wanted to get something easy that can be fun to use. I remember, when as a child I attended a club of martial arts and the coach said: you need to learn and hone one hold so that you like it and feel yourself the best in it. And then you can learn more advanced techniques, i.e., step by step, and never in a hurry. The comfort will come, but only with practice. I remember these words, which often help me in life - step by step, without a rush.

Purely by chance I met IF on the site FF, and I began to read his thread (read the market). So, I came to the site RTM. Having experience, even segmental, for 2-3 months I swallowed as a machine the journals of Traders... I was so engrossed that I started and ended the day with RTM. It seems intuitively I knew that there I would find what I was looking for.

Then I took a break for two weeks, I did not want to get used to it. Then I started doing homework, as advised on the site. After about 5 months I finally realized that I had found what I was looking for. And I found the following: All the beauty of the market can be read only in terms of pure chart and without any indicators, pure chart only. A thought flashed - it is the same like the doctor reads cardiogram. He can determine the problems with heart, using simple diagram.

It takes about six months to learn the material on this site.

I wrote «Beauty is in the simplicity» at the bottom of my nickname, for the reason that I like to find the simple things that work. I really liked the last posts of Benhur, which confirmed that I am on the right way: look for simple things on the market - this is the main. You have to believe in the main point: the beauty is in the simplicity of the market. And the Grail in this business is Patience. I often say, the grass grows without our efforts. Indeed, our experience, thanks to my favorite site (RTM), is growing itself. And you know, in order to get PATIENCE - you should not wait or demand anything from the market, don’t wait that the market goes towards you. Just hone simple things and use them.

It is very important to create your own journal and put charts in order to improve your skills.

Just wanted to share my experience. Today I'm looking for simple things, and you can see from my posts that I am using the simple things, and they work. Today I am a profitable trader. I do not demand from the market ANYTHING, I just like to look at the chart and have fun as PRO makes money. And one more thing: do not put the goal of making money instantly.

Let the grass grows by itself without your efforts. I hope you understand me. Beauty is in simplicity.

Many thanks to IF and team of Masters-Traders for creating an excellent communication here. This stuff really works.

I hope I helped you a bit on your way to becoming a trader, good luck!!!!!!!
Nice and refreshing post, Thanks a million. Hope to reach same soon.

We could be twins! I started with Trading Chaos. No live money only demo. Then Eliot wave analysis; demo. Then PA at S/R i.e. Nial Fuller; demo. Then ratios and harmonics at S/D with small live account; break even. This was where I learned about the engulf. As soon as IF explained the engulf and why it works in the correct places I absolutely knew this was the only "correct" place and that all other methods were subsets of this one directly or indirectly.

I've confirmed this week that I'm not struggling with emotion at all I'm struggling with reading correctly or gaining experience. If I don't' know what to expect when I trade certain areas the root of the problem is not emotion. Emotion is the result of not having the experience to know what being right and being wrong looks like on the chart. Now that I know its not a problem with "me" I've been attacking the root and learning what the market can do at my entry points and what a good vs bad trade looks like.

I agree with you fully. Let the grass grow and be patient; this is expert advice. I've only traded 4 times this week but each trade was a value trade and although I'm BE a lot I'm learning from each one.

Thanks so much for sharing your experience. It strengthens my resolve to reach my dream of trading full time just like you. As you know I love your charts. Cheers.
